title: From Winning to Giving: The Effect of Gold Medals in Crowdsourcing Contests
authors: Shan Liu; Fan Zhang; Jing Wang; Baojun Gao
eligible_reason: Main identification is a regression discontinuity at the medal rank cutoffs (rdrobust; Tables 3-4, Figures 4-5; abstract: 'Employing a regression discontinuity design'). The only DiD analyses are appendix robustness checks: Table A20 / Figure A5 (5.RobustnessChecks/AlternativeIdentification_DID_Code.do) and Appendix E surprise-gold (6.SurpriseGold/SurpriseGold_Code.do). Both are user x relative-week panels around each focal contest: reghdfe y winner after treatafter, a(userid weekindex competitionid), where weekindex is relative week (-15..15), not calendar time, and after = weekindex >= 0 is defined for all users at their own contest date (extra treatment regressor; competition FE are an extra additive FE). No calendar-time FE, appendix-only. Not an eligible design.
design_notes: R rdrobust/rdlocrand for main results; Stata reghdfe for appendix DiD. DiD data AlternativeIdentification_DID_Data.csv: UserId, CompetitionId, Winner (gold medal in focal contest), WeekIndex (relative week), outcomes Participation, PostProb, log_Volume, log_Length, log_Votes; vce(robust).
main_or_robustness: robustness (DiD in online appendix only; main design is RDD)
data_files_note: Scraped platform (Kaggle-type ML competition) data shipped as CSVs; README states all data needed are included.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). RDD paper; appendix DiD uses relative-week FE and a per-user after indicator.
